title: Tadoba Dawn Canopy // Sector 4B Morning Light
claim: Early morning light breaking through the dry deciduous teak canopy of Tadoba-Andhari. Sunlight pierces through the foliage, illuminating the dense woodland corridor where Bengal tigers establish territorial trails. Captured at 06:39 AM during our field study, setting the environmental benchmark for camera-trap illumination.

title: Forest Flank Corridor // Dappled Canopy Shadow
claim: Dappled shadow patterns dancing across the forest floor as morning rays penetrate the teak canopy. This extreme contrast between direct sun and heavy shade highlights the core computational challenge: extracting invariant stripe bifurcations when ambient lighting creates false boundaries across an animal's flanks.

title: Moharli Core Trail // Horizon Depth Vector
claim: Looking outward through the dense teak corridor toward the horizon as the morning mist burns away. The rugged terrain and tangled branch structures demonstrate why automated segmentation must isolate the animal cleanly from background foliage. A foundational habitat plate for our simulated environment benchmarks.

title: Canopy Silhouette // Vertical Geometry Benchmark
claim: Twin prominent teak trunks standing tall against the luminous morning sky, casting long linear shadows. In our Blender GroveScape simulations, we used these precise vertical tree silhouettes and branch densities to parametrically model realistic occlusions for the 10,000 synthetic training scenes.

title: Teak Trunk Bifurcations // Natural Graph Topology
claim: Intertwined forest trunks and branching patterns photographed in the early hours near the Moharli gate. The fractal branching of deciduous teak trees provided inspiration for our graph-based stripe representation: treating fur bifurcations as persistent topological vertices rather than static pixel grids.

title: Deep Corridor View // Foreshortened Perspective
claim: A perspective view through the forest corridor capturing angular foreshortening and foliage layering. When a tiger turns or steps uphill, body perspective changes dramatically across camera-trap views. This plate served as our reference for tuning 3D pose-estimation keypoints under severe viewing angles.

title: The Living Forest // Epilogue Specimen Plate
claim: Warm golden light bathing the forest floor through the canopy in a moment of quiet stillness. The closing visual of our journey: a reminder that behind every biometric vector and segmentation mask lies an ancient, living ecosystem. ‘The forest has a memory. We are learning to read it.’

title: Stage Q&A // Defending the Algorithmic Pipeline

Engaging in a genuine dialogue about the future of Indian conservation technology.

title: Biometric Pipeline Channels // Feature Extraction Evidence
claim: 08:08 AM: Live telemetry capture showing our 5-stage feature extraction workflow in action. From left to right: raw camera frame, high-precision segmentation mask, 3D pose skeletal keypoints, and normalized planar stripe vector. The technical foundation of WildID proven live on local test images.

title: Planar Vector Representation // Stripe Geometry Map
claim: 08:10 AM: Inspecting the unwrapped 2D fur-carpet coordinate space extracted from test plates. By flattening the animal's flank onto a standardized planar template, our model eliminated pose-induced distortions. This enabled vector similarity lookups to run in under 40 milliseconds against the stored database.

title: Territory Roaming Polygons // Spatial Telemetry Engine
claim: 09:51 AM: Testing the spatial roaming engine across Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve sectors. Translating individual re-identification matches into dynamic convex hull territorial polygons on an interactive map. Proving that WildID goes beyond classification to provide longitudinal ecological intelligence.

title: Leaflet GIS Command Dashboard // Live Operations Center
claim: 10:05 AM: The interactive WildID Operations Center running live with Leaflet GIS mapping. Range officers can inspect verified sightings, click on territorial centroids, and view historical movements across Moharli and Kolsa sectors. The centerpiece of our live presentation to the judging panel.

title: Ecological Corridor Analytics // Water Basin Correlation
claim: 10:34 AM: Correlating tiger sighting densities with seasonal water availability along the Andheri River basin. Demonstrating how multi-observation telemetry flags potential territorial shifts caused by summer drought or prey migration. A decision-support tool tailored directly for forest conservators.
